Q: How to Populate an Unbound Field in Access Report With Specific Text A:

Without knowing the full details of your report, I would say that the Report_Load event is probably not the right place to be doing these checks. To solve your issue, create a private function in your report module with the code below. You can include additional checks as per the code itself:

Private Function fErrorTextBox(strSpecificCitation As String, _
                               strGeneralCitation As String, _
                               strEmissionPoint As String)

  If strSpecificCitation = "" Then
    fErrorTextBox = "Missing Specific Citation"

  ElseIf strGeneralCitation = "" Then
    fErrorTextBox = "Missing General Citation"

  ElseIf strEmissionPoint = "" Then
    fErrorTextBox = "Missing Emmission Point"

  Else
    fErrorTextBox = ""

  End If

End Function

Place the following in the control source of the textbox:

=fErrorTextBox(Nz(SpecificCitation), Nz(GeneralCitation), Nz(EmissionPoint))

You need to include the Nz function or the report will fail because VBA does not like null values being passed into a function.

Q: Outlook VBA: How to select a mail folder manually and return the name to the code A:

If the code below is not working in Outlook 2010, then the PickFolder method is available and easier to code, though it doesn't give the same user experience as the one you're looking for. See for example: Outlook VBA Pickfolder command to include subfolders

In Outlook 365 this works for me inside a non-modal form:

Option Explicit

Public WithEvents myOlExp As Outlook.Explorer

Private Sub UserForm_Activate()
    Set myOlExp = Application.ActiveExplorer
End Sub

Private Sub myOlExp_Activate()
    GetSelection "Activate"
End Sub
Private Sub myOlExp_SelectionChange()
    GetSelection "Change"
End Sub

Private Sub GetSelection(EventType As String)
    If myOlExp.Selection.Count = 0 Then
        DoMsg EventType & ": " & myOlExp.CurrentFolder.Name
    Else
        DoMsg EventType & ": " & TypeName(myOlExp.Selection(1)) & " in '" & _
              myOlExp.Selection(1).Parent.Name & "'"
    End If
End Sub

Private Sub DoMsg(msg As String)
    Me.Label1.Caption = msg
End Sub

Seems to give the desired result (when clicking around in my mailbox)

Action Debug output
Activate Outlook Activate: MailItem in 'Inbox'
Select folder "Drafts" Change: Drafts, Change: MailItem in 'Drafts'
Select folder "Junk Email" Change: Junk Email, Change: MailItem in 'Junk Email'
Select folder "Personal" Change: Personal, Change: MailItem in 'Personal'

Q: Build/Automate Excel table with empty rows as separator A:

A solution independent from any column names

let
    Source = Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name="Table1"]}[Content],
    Cols = Table.ColumnNames(Source),
    #"Grouped Table" = Table.Group(Source, Cols{0}, {"grp", each let val=Table.ToColumns(_){0}{0} in #table(Cols, {{val, null}}) & Table.SelectColumns(_, Cols{1})}),
    #"Expanded grp" = Table.ExpandTableColumn(Table.SelectColumns(#"Grouped Table", "grp"), "grp", Cols)
in
    #"Expanded grp"

Q: Count consecutive rows in MySQL A:

This is gaps and islands problem. Try the following and here is the demo in MySql 8.0.

select
    id
from
(   
  select
        diff_chck,
        id,
        count(*) over (partition by diff_chck, rnk) as total
    from
    (
        select
            diff_chck,
            id,
            id - row_number() over (partition by diff_chck order by id) as rnk
        from myTable
    ) t
) vals
where total > 2

order by
    id

Output:

*-----*
| id  |
*-----*
| 5   |
| 6   |
| 7   |
| 8   |
*-----*

Q: Kafka can not delete old log segments on Windows A:

The main problem is that on Windows, old log files cannot be deleted while they are still being used by the main Kafka thread. Linux uses different filesystem semantics, so this issue does not occur there.

Root cause: The lock failures are caused by the use of different Java APIs to open files. In some cases, Kafka uses RandomAccessFile, while in others it uses FileChannel.open(). On Windows, opening files with RandomAccessFile does not set the FILE_SHARE_DELETE flag, which results in “access denied” errors when attempting to rename or delete open files. In contrast, FileChannel.open() sets FILE_SHARE_DELETE by default (confirmed on JDK 8 and 11), as noted in a comment by Maksim Zinal.

Solution: The issue is addressed by KAFKA-1194, implemented in a pull request to the apache/kafka repository. However, this fix has not been merged into the main branch. At the time of writing this comment, the Kafka version is 4.1. As a workaround, you can pull that branch locally and build Kafka from source.
